source: AI Agent Orchestration Trends Nov 2026 (general survey)
summary: General survey of multi-agent orchestration trends: hybrid rule-based/generative models, governance layers, cryptographically verifiable execution, and enterprise adoption at ~23% past pilots.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — no specific novel technique beyond what AgentForge already implements. Error handling, retries, and observability flagged as needed are already tracked in HID-163/167/186.

summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' as compounding leverage from agent tooling (subagents, memory, permissions, MCP, skills). Also ran an 8-agent parallel experiment that reportedly failed.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — confirms AgentForge's existing design. Parallel agent execution experiment failure reinforces deliberate rejection of parallel execution in AgentForge. No new gap identified.

summary: LangGraph's LangMem provides three memory types (semantic, episodic, procedural) backed by PostgresStore. Core launch was Oct 2024; 2026 updates focus on hosted checkpointers and cross-thread stores.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already shipped skill distillation (agentSkillRepository.ts/distillationAgent.ts). Cross-run episodic memory is already tracked by open issue HID-188.

source: Reflexion / Self-Improving Agent Reflection Pattern (open source, 2026 roundup)
summary: Reflexion is a pattern where agents review past actions/outcomes and update prompts or internal state. Now mainstream in LangGraph/CrewAI/AutoGen. Works best with verifiable outcomes (code with tests).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge has skill distillation as a form of reflection. Adversarial plan critique (a related concept) is tracked in open issue HID-93.

source: INTENT: Inference-Time Budget-Constrained Tool Use (arXiv Feb 2026)
summary: INTENT is an inference-time planner using a learned world model and Monte Carlo lookahead to enforce hard budget constraints on tool use. Found standalone agents often violate budget constraints.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — confirms value of token/cost telemetry but requires telemetry data to exist first. Already blocked on HID-163 (per-run token cost and stage latency telemetry). Not actionable until HID-163 ships.

summary: Tests whether LLM agents can predict their own remaining spend. Finds budget awareness decouples from task performance and can be trained as a control signal (early-stop policy).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to HID-163 (token cost telemetry). Not actionable until telemetry infrastructure exists and HID-163 is shipped.

source: Agent Checkpoint & Partial Retry Patterns (practitioner blogs, Apr-May 2026)
summary: Practitioner guidance on partial-failure recovery: checkpoint before/after each step, idempotency keys, saga-style compensation, small units of work. Confirms retries need externalized state.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — HID-186 (stage-level partial retry via earliest-failure-point detection) and HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification) already cover these patterns.

summary: No new Oct/Nov 2026 releases found for AutoGen or Magentic-One. Latest documented work shows version bumps on magentic-one-cli package with dependency bound changes only.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — no novel capability introduced. Magentic-One's multi-agent team structure already reviewed and out-of-scope for AgentForge's CLI-subprocess model.
